bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42488035 (fluent-bit): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 found by fuzz target flb-it-fuzz-msgpack_parse_fuzzer_OSSFUZZ [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42488035
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced the saved AddressSanitizer crash against the staged vulnerable checkout in `_work/src/fluent-bit`, whose `HEAD` is the ancestor revision `6fe5d030bcee43556fb1c6054f55854c605a5b0c` rather than the later metadata commit `e5289e606c4b55b0fac29046c8343958248189e7`. The staged runtime warning `[pack] invalid UTF-8 bytes, skipping` and the vulnerable lines in `src/flb_pack.c:604-605` and `src/flb_utils.c:683-720` match this staged ancestor exactly. In that source, `flb_msgpack_raw_to_json_sds()` derives the first JSON buffer as `out_size = in_size * 1.5`, so the staged 512-byte witness gets an initial 768-byte SDS buffer and `flb_msgpack_to_json()` converts with `json_size - 1 == 767` content bytes. `msgpack_unpack_next()` consumes only the first 287 bytes as a 15-entry root map whose nested root-entry-3 value contains the 5-byte string `f4 81 81 81 81`. Late in the first conversion attempt, that string reaches `flb_utils_write_str()` with only 6 content bytes left. On the staged signed-`char` path, `0xf4` enters the `c > 0xFFFF` arm, `flb_utf8_len()` returns 4, `flb_utf8_decode()` accepts `f4 81 81 81` as codepoint `0x101041`, and `snprintf("\\u%04x", codepoint)` returns the 8-byte escape `\u101041`. Because the vulnerable helper only checks `available - written < 6` before copying `len` bytes, it emits those 8 bytes into the remaining 6, `available - written` wraps as unsigned `size_t`, the trailing `0x81` is handled as a separate 1-byte invalid sequence that triggers `[pack] invalid UTF-8 bytes, skipping`, and the helper returns with `*off == 769`. The closing quote write then fails, `msgpack2json()` returns false, yet `flb_msgpack_to_json()` still executes `json_str[off] = '\0';` at index 769, matching the saved `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at `src/flb_pack.c:605`. The metadata fix commit `979a9bb728b490659e7e6076c17f3e4cb2c5bd59` expresses the missing obligation by adding `if ((available - written) < len) return FLB_FALSE;` before each `encoded_to_buf(...)` call in `flb_utils_write_str()`.

source.description: Source. This is the first project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled witness into the `msgpack_object` tree later traversed by the vulnerable JSON writer.
source.value_from: The staged file `gt_results/arvo_42488035/poc` is exactly 512 bytes (sha256 `c92a9442aa3f16352addb44105f860741623e07883bd658d433069b46f9d93b0`). The harness forwards input to `flb_msgpack_raw_to_json_sds(data, size)` only when `size == 512`. Static MsgPack decoding shows `msgpack_unpack_next()` consumes the first 287 bytes as a 15-entry root map; inside root entry 3's nested value is the 5-byte `str` `f4 81 81 81 81` that later reaches `flb_utils_write_str()`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After the helper has already advanced `off` to 769 and the closing quote write has failed, this unconditional terminator write stores one byte past the JSON buffer.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at `src/flb_pack.c:605` in `flb_msgpack_to_json`, 0 bytes to the right of the 785-byte SDS allocation created from the initial 768-byte `out_size`, with `flb_msgpack_raw_to_json_sds` and `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` immediately below it in the stack.

root_cause.description: In the signed-`char` high-byte UTF-8 branch, the staged helper only checks for 6 free bytes before formatting `\u%04x`, so a call with 6 bytes left still proceeds even when `snprintf()` returns `len == 8`.
root_cause.note: The fix commit `979a9bb728b490659e7e6076c17f3e4cb2c5bd59` adds the missing `if ((available - written) < len) return FLB_FALSE;` immediately after each `snprintf(...)` in this helper.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled witness length becomes the first JSON-buffer capacity. For the staged 512-byte PoC, this sets `out_size = 768`, so `flb_msgpack_to_json()` later makes its first conversion attempt with `left = 767` content bytes.

parser_admitted.description: The 512-byte witness is accepted as a MsgPack object by `msgpack_unpack_next()`, so `flb_msgpack_raw_to_json_sds()` proceeds directly into `flb_msgpack_to_json()` on the materialized root object.

fine_trace.note: The staged harness only forwards 512-byte inputs. For this witness, `in_size == 512`, so the first SDS JSON buffer is allocated with `out_size == 768`; `sds_alloc()` adds the 16-byte header and trailing NUL that ASan later reports as a 785-byte region.

Source. This statement parses the attacker-controlled bytes into the `msgpack_object` tree later traversed by the JSON writer. Static decoding shows the first unpacked object is a 15-entry root map and that root entry 3 contains the nested 5-byte `str` `f4 81 81 81 81`.

fine_trace.code:
if (try_to_write(buf, off, left, "\"", 1) &&
    (o->via.str.size > 0 ?
     try_to_write_str(buf, off, left, o->via.str.ptr, o->via.str.size)

    try_to_write(buf, off, left, "\"", 1)) {
fine_trace.note: On the first conversion attempt, `flb_msgpack_to_json()` has passed `left = json_size - 1 = 767` into `msgpack2json()`. By the time recursion reaches the nested 5-byte string from step 1, earlier output has advanced `*off` to 760; the opening quote at line 487 makes `*off == 761`, so `flb_utils_write_str()` starts with `available = size - *off = 6` and `required = str_len = 5`.

With signed `char`, the leading `0xf4` is promoted into the `c > 0xFFFF` branch. Here `flb_utf8_len(0xf4)` returns 4, `flb_utf8_decode()` accepts `f4 81 81 81` as codepoint `0x101041`, and `snprintf()` formats that codepoint as the 8-byte escape `\u101041`.

Root cause. At this call site `available - written == 6`, so the fixed 6-byte guard passes even though step 3 has already made the real copy length `len == 8`. The helper has no `available - written < len` check to stop and let the caller reallocate.

`encoded_to_buf()` still copies all 8 bytes with only 6 content bytes left. `written` becomes 8 while `available` was 6, so the next `available - written` evaluation is unsigned `size_t` underflow instead of a negative remainder.

The trailing `0x81` is then processed as a separate 1-byte invalid sequence. Because step 5 wrapped `available - written`, the size checks no longer fire; this branch emits the saved warning, breaks, and then line 720 adds `written` to the caller offset, moving `*off` from 761 to 769 while still returning `FLB_TRUE`.

Back in the `MSGPACK_OBJECT_STR` case, the closing quote write now fails because `left == 767` and `*off == 769`. `msgpack2json()` therefore returns `FLB_FALSE` for this first conversion attempt instead of reaching the reallocation loop with a clean in-bounds failure.

Sink. `flb_msgpack_to_json()` executes this store unconditionally after line 604 returns. With `off == 769`, it writes one byte past the 768-byte content buffer into the 785-byte SDS allocation reported by ASan.

allocation_context.note: ASan shows the overflowed 785-byte heap region originates from this `flb_sds_create_size(out_size)` call.

format.name: Exact 512-byte MsgPack witness whose first unpacked object contains the failing `f4 81 81 81 81` string
format.contract: Exactly the staged file `gt_results/arvo_42488035/poc` (sha256 `c92a9442aa3f16352addb44105f860741623e07883bd658d433069b46f9d93b0`). The harness rejects every non-512-byte input. In the staged vulnerable checkout, `msgpack_unpack_next()` consumes only the first 287 bytes as the first MsgPack object. That object contains a nested 5-byte `str` `f4 81 81 81 81`; on the signed-`char` path, the first four bytes become codepoint `0x101041`, the trailing `81` is a separate invalid 1-byte sequence that triggers the saved warning, the final `flb_utils_write_str()` call starts with only 6 content bytes left in the initial 768-byte buffer, and the crash occurs when `flb_msgpack_to_json()` later executes `json_str[769] = '\0'`.
